summary: Quantify whether the two rounding fixes matter: ablation experiments, math verification, removal cost

ablation.summary: Tom is RIGHT. The anti-windup change (25% integral clamp + back-calculation) is the entire fix; both rounding changes are behaviorally inert. In the kI sweep, anti-windup alone (step2 with both roundings reverted via --floor-output --sticky-decay) kills the limit cycles exactly as well as full step2: old firmware posts post_move_rms of 2,500-4,400 counts at kI>=10, while AW-only posts medians of 39-107 counts, statistically indistinguishable from full step2's 45-82 (differences are seed noise; per-seed scatter within each config is larger than any between-config gap). Snap-back overshoot: old = ~24,000 counts, all three step2 variants = 2,760-2,910 counts, spread across variants (~150) equal to spread across seeds (~80). R2 (sticky D-decay fix) only cleans an internal debug value: the sticky bias scales linearly with kD (ss_d_mean ~= -0.48*kD pre-shift: -85k at kD=175k up to -662k at kD=1.4M) yet tick-level CSV comparison over 187,500 standstill ticks shows ZERO position differences at both kD=175k and kD=1.4M, and ss_i_mean/ss_err_std/max_abs_error are identical to the digit — the DC output bias (up to 663 counts at kD=1.4M, ~42 at production kD) sits below stiction breakaway and never reaches the plant. R1 (round-to-nearest output) changes the output by at most 1 LSB (max |delta|=1 on 244/500 ticks, position identical on all 500) and move performance is identical within noise (median 50.3 vs 49.4). Neither rounding fix has any measurable effect on motor behavior; neither is harmful either — they are cosmetic correctness polish, not fixes.
ablation.verdict: CONFIRMED: anti-windup alone is the fix. R1 (output rounding): NO measurable behavioral effect (max 1 LSB, zero position divergence, performance within seed noise). R2 (D-decay fix): NO measurable behavioral effect (zero position difference over 187,500 ticks even at 8x production kD); it only removes a bias in the internal/debug D-term value.
details:
EXP1 HEADLINE - post_move_rms (counts), 2 rot / 2 s move, 8 s duration, kp=2000 kd=175000, seeds 1-5. Format: median / max.
| kI  | old (median/max) | AW-only (median/max) | AW+R1 (median/max) | full step2 (median/max) |
|-----|------------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------------|
| 5   | 39.3 / 2799.8    | 39.3 / 103.8         | 164.5 / 384.6      | 44.7 / 241.2            |
| 10  | 3606.4 / 4355.7  | 43.2 / 117.7         | 63.1 / 115.6       | 81.6 / 119.6            |
| 25  | 3742.1 / 4000.4  | 52.9 / 68.8          | 54.9 / 195.8       | 50.3 / 119.3            |
| 50  | 2655.5 / 2739.9  | 77.9 / 297.2         | 77.6 / 485.2       | 61.1 / 93.9             |
| 100 | 2479.9 / 2537.5  | 106.9 / 140.9        | 64.8 / 141.2       | 60.8 / 88.3             |
Reading: old limit-cycles catastrophically at kI>=10 (and 1/5 seeds even at kI=5). AW-only is as good as full step2 at every kI; which variant 'wins' flips sign with kI and is pure seed noise (per-seed values range 33-485 in ALL step2 variants). Anti-windup alone is sufficient.

EXP2 tick-level proof (seed 1, 6 s standstill = 187,500 ticks, --csv --decimate 1): kD=175000: position differs on 0/187500 ticks, while output differs on 187496 ticks (max |dOut|=67 counts, mean pre-shift |dD|=85059 ~= 41.5 counts post-shift-11). kD=1400000: position differs on 0/187500 ticks, output differs on 187476 ticks (max |dOut|=663 counts, mean pre-shift |dD|=675095 ~= 330 counts post-shift). The sticky D-bias produces a genuine DC offset in the commanded output voltage, but even the 8x-production worst case (330-663 counts) stays below the static-friction breakaway of the bench-calibrated plant, so the rotor never moves and the error/integral streams are unchanged. Caveat worth one sentence: this DC drive bias means slightly asymmetric standstill drive (a small constant voltage push) which could in principle matter as extra holding current/heat or near-breakaway margin at very high kD - but at production kD=175000 it is ~42/2048 counts of authority and unmeasurable at position level.

EXP3 - R1 (round-to-nearest vs floor on output shift). (a) Performance, ki=25, move 2 rot/2 s, seeds 1-5: step2 = 38.4/119.3/50.3/62.5/40.7 (median 50.3, max 119.3); step2 --floor-output = 54.5/49.4/37.6/61.8/49.2 (median 49.4, max 61.8). Identical within seed noise (floor's nominally lower max is not meaningful - see EXP1 scatter). (b) Tick-by-tick, 1 s standstill, seed 1, first 500 ticks: max |delta output| = 1 count, exactly as expected; delta histogram {0: 256 ticks, 1: 244 ticks}; error column identical on 500/500 ticks, i.e. the +-1 LSB output difference produced ZERO position divergence even while it was present on 49% of ticks.

EXP4 - snap-back 0.61-rot instant step, ki=25 kd=350000, duration 4, overshoot_counts for seeds 1/3/6:
| config     | seed1 | seed3 | seed6 |
|------------|-------|-------|-------|
| old        | 24019 | 24010 | 24005 |
| AW-only    | 2875  | 2824  | 2832  |
| AW+R1      | 2858  | 2761  | 2832  |
| full step2 | 2883  | 2831  | 2910  |
Old overshoots ~24,000 counts (windup); every step2 variant lands at 2,760-2,910. Between-variant spread (~150 counts) equals within-variant seed spread (~80-100 counts): no difference beyond noise. Anti-windup is again the whole story.

VERDICT R1 (output round-to-nearest): NO measurable effect on motor behavior. It changes the output by at most 1 LSB, produced zero position divergence over 500 observed ticks, and move performance is seed-noise-identical. Keep it or drop it on code-taste grounds only.

VERDICT R2 (D-filter round-toward-zero decay): NO measurable effect on motor behavior in any experiment - position trajectories are bit-identical over 187,500-tick standstill runs even at 8x production kD, and all position/integral metrics match to the digit. What it DOES fix is the internal D-term debug/telemetry value (removes a bias of ~0.48*kD pre-shift, ~-85k at production gains) and a small DC offset in commanded standstill drive that stiction fully absorbs. Worth keeping only for honest debug captures and high-kD headroom, not as a behavioral fix.

BOTTOM LINE: Tom's intuition is CONFIRMED on all four experiments. The anti-windup change (25% integral clamp + back-calculation) is the fix - it alone eliminates the kI limit cycles (median rms 39-107 vs old's 2,480-3,742) and cuts snap-back overshoot 8.5x. The two rounding changes are correctness polish with no bench-observable effect; they are also harmless, so reverting them buys nothing except a smaller diff.

Simulator: prebuilt pid_sim (bench-calibrated plant, deterministic seeds); step2 = current firmware algorithm, --floor-output reverts R1, --sticky-decay reverts R2. No repo files modified.

math.summary: Tom is half right. R1 (output-shift round-to-nearest) is provably a <=1-count cosmetic change: exhaustive check over all int32 sums shows floor vs round differ by exactly 0 or 1, and even through the anti-windup feedback path the two variants' integral terms never diverge by more than exactly 1 output count (2048 pre-shift) over 5e6 simulated ticks -- it does not accumulate and the position integrator absorbs the static -0.5-count bias. R2 (D-filter decay fix) is NOT a 1-count issue: the floor decay's stuck set is exactly {-31..-1} (proven and verified exhaustively), producing an expected standstill D-term bias of -84,813 pre-shift (-41.4 output counts) at stock kD=175000 -- matching Tom's bench measurement of ~-85,000 -- and up to -83 counts worst case, scaling linearly with kD (-662 counts at kD=1.4M). The position loop's integral cancels it at steady state, so what R2 actually fixes is tuning observability (debug D-term reads -85k at standstill), direction-asymmetric settling (bias is always negative), and integrator re-slew bumps whenever the random rest value or kD changes. Verdict: keep both (they're free), but only R2 fixes a real measurable defect; R1 is genuinely cosmetic; the anti-windup remains the only fix relevant to the original limit-cycle problem.
details: R1 arithmetic claim PROVEN: for s = q*2^k + r (0 <= r < 2^k), floor((s+2^(k-1))/2^k) - floor(s/2^k) = (r >= 2^(k-1)) which is 0 or 1, always. Verified exhaustively in C over ALL 2^32 int32 values for k=11 (M17): min diff 0, max diff 1. Average bias over a full residue period: floor = -0.4998 output counts, round = +0.0002 counts. Program: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tom-Documents-Move-the-Needle-Servomotor-firmware/74e569b6-9702-4e05-a09d-9f128c5923f8/scratchpad/ultra/r1_exhaustive.c

R1 system-level question (output fed back via anti-windup at motor_control.c:2379-2394) RESOLVED as BOUNDED, not accumulating: dual simulation of the exact M17 integer controller (kp=2000, ki=5, kd=175000, shift=11, limit=51200) on identical error sequences -- deep +/- saturation square wave plus noise plus near-limit dithering, 5e6 ticks of which 3.47e6 saturated -- shows max |I_floor - I_round| = exactly 2048 pre-shift = 1.000 output count, and max output difference = 1 count. Reason: the AW back-calculation recomputes the excess fresh from current state every tick (proportional feedback on the excess, not an integration of it), so rounding residue has no memory to accumulate in; it only offsets the integrator's equilibrium band by <= 1 LSB. Outside saturation output_value is a pure function of state and is never fed back, so floor is a static -0.5-count DC offset which the position loop's integral term absorbs. Program: scratchpad/ultra/r1_saturation_divergence.c

R2(a) PROVEN: (x*(S-1)) >> log2(S) = x + floor(-x/S), so fixed points are exactly floor(-x/S)=0, i.e. -(S-1) <= x <= 0; for S=32 the pathological stuck set is exactly {-31..-1} (0 is the legitimate rest point). Verified exhaustively in C over x in [-70e6, +70e6], which covers the full reachable filter range (|lpf| <= 32 * max_error_change <= 64e6): exactly 32 fixed points, range [-31..0]; the firmware's round-toward-zero correction has 0 as its only fixed point and decays to 0 from every start; positive values decay fine under both. Program: scratchpad/ultra/r2_stuck_set.c

R2(b) worst-case persistent pre-shift bias = -(S-1)*(kD>>5): kD=175000 -> -169,508 pre-shift = -82.8 output counts (0.16% of 51200 authority; 0.40% of the 20480 authority at the M17 default 80 PWM-voltage); kD=350000 -> -165.6 counts (0.32%); kD=700000 -> -331.1 (0.65%); kD=1.4e6 -> -662.2 (1.29%); kD=u32 max (firmware caps to INT32_MAX at motor_control.c:2157) -> -2,080,374,753 pre-shift = -1,015,808 counts, i.e. the stuck D bias alone rails the output. Scaling is linear in kD.

R2(c) expected (not worst-case) resting bias, simulated 1e6 ticks with white error noise sigma=38 counts/tick (error_change sigma ~54): floor decay rests at mean lpf = -15.51 -> mean d_term = -84,813 pre-shift = -41.4 output counts (0.081% of 51200; 0.20% of 20480). This matches Tom's bench-measured ~-85,000 pre-shift almost exactly -- independent confirmation of both the mechanism and the noise model. Corrected decay: mean d_term -16 pre-shift = -0.01 counts. When noise stops entirely, floor-decay rest values across 2000 trials span the full stuck set [-31..0], mean -15.4. Program: scratchpad/ultra/r2_noise_sim.py

R2(d) what the position loop's integral does NOT compensate: (1) tuning observability -- the READ_PID_DEBUG_DATA derivative_term (motor_control.c:2401) reads ~-85,000 at standstill, corrupting any measurement-based tuning (this is exactly how the bug was noticed); (2) direction asymmetry -- the bias is strictly negative (stuck set is one-sided), so +/- direction transients see different effective D and settle asymmetrically; (3) re-slew transients -- the rest value is a random element of {-31..0} that changes after every disturbance, and steps instantly by (delta_kd>>5)*lpf_stuck on a runtime Set-PID-constants, forcing the integrator (ki=5) to re-slew up to ~83 counts each time -> small position bumps/settling wobble; (4) it consumes ~41 of the 12800-count (25%) integral clamp headroom -- negligible (0.3%). Steady-state position accuracy itself is unaffected because the integrator cancels any constant output bias.

Ranking, explicit per Tom's question: R1 -- Tom is RIGHT; it is exactly an error-of-1-in-the-output issue (proven <=1 count, non-accumulating even at saturation through the AW path, mean effect half a count); harmless to keep since it costs one add. R2 -- Tom is WRONG that it is a 1-count issue; it is a 41-count expected / 83-count worst-case persistent output bias at stock gains (his own -85,000 pre-shift measurement confirms it), growing linearly with kD, with real if second-order system consequences (debug-data corruption, asymmetric settling, re-slew bumps). Neither R1 nor R2 addresses the original limit-cycle problem -- the 25% integral clamp + back-calculation anti-windup remains the only meaningful fix for THAT -- but R2 is an independently real defect fix, not a rounding nicety.

Firmware references: output rounding R1 at /Users/tom/Documents/Move_the_Needle/Servomotor/firmware/Src/motor_control.c:2370; D-decay fix R2 at motor_control.c:2337-2341; anti-windup at 2379-2394; the OLD floor-decay form still visible in the #if 0 legacy controller at 2465 and old output shift at 2485. Constants: PID_SHIFT_RIGHT=11 (M17, motor_control.h:100), scalar S=32 (shift 5, motor_control.h:112), kD default 175000 (motor_control.h:80), kd>>5 = 5468, M17 default max PWM voltage 80 (motor_control.h:127) -> default authority 20480 counts (51200 corresponds to voltage 200). All verification programs in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tom-Documents-Move-the-Needle-Servomotor-firmware/74e569b6-9702-4e05-a09d-9f128c5923f8/scratchpad/ultra/ (r1_exhaustive.c, r1_saturation_divergence.c, r2_stuck_set.c, r2_noise_sim.py); no repo files modified.
math.verdict: R1 (output round-to-nearest): Tom is right -- provably <=1 count, non-accumulating, cosmetic. R2 (D-filter decay fix): Tom is wrong -- it fixes a real, measured ~41-count (expected) / 83-count (worst-case) persistent D-term output bias at stock kD, linear in kD, whose uncompensated effects are debug-data corruption, direction-asymmetric settling, and integrator re-slew bumps. The anti-windup remains the only fix relevant to the original limit-cycle problem; R2 is a legitimate independent bug fix; R1 is polish.

removal.summary: Removal-cost inventory for R1 (output round-to-nearest) and R2 (D-filter decay round-toward-zero): removing either requires coordinated edits in 3 mirrored models (differential reference, overflow shadow, sim step2) plus the firmware, an ablation-flag inversion in the sim, check rewrites in run_pid_sim_battery.py and hw_campaign.py (R2 only — its removal makes two existing gates FAIL by design), a plan-doc addendum, a firmware version bump + rebuild + release files, and a full gate re-run (~25-40 min offline + ~1 h bench). Nothing breaks in pid_debug_capture.py or archived captures — detect_shift auto-detects floor vs round-nearest per capture. Keep cost is ~7 executed instructions (~0.1 µs of the 32 µs tick, ~0.3% of ISR budget). R1 is honestly near-free to remove behaviorally (±1 count, and the integrator absorbs it whenever kI>0; PID_controller_debug at motor_control.c:2284 still uses floor anyway). R2 removal reinstates a real measured artifact (wandering −85k pre-shift D bias = ~−40 counts of output torque command; a ~40-count standing position offset when kI=0) and requires weakening the H10 hardware gate and two battery checks — which collides with Tom's own fix-bugs-not-tests rule.
removal.verdict: R1 removal: cheap behaviorally, expensive procedurally (5 code sites + docs + full gate re-run for a ±1-count effect either way). R2 removal: everything R1 needs PLUS it deliberately re-introduces a measured defect and forces weakening the hw_campaign H10 gate (abs(d_mean)<40000 fails at ~−85k) and two battery checks. Keeping both costs ~7 instructions ≈ 0.1 µs/tick. On pure cost-benefit, removal buys ~0.3% ISR headroom for hours of re-verification; if minimalism is still wanted, R1 alone is the defensible cut, R2 is not.
details: FIRMWARE (/Users/tom/Documents/Move_the_Needle/Servomotor/firmware/Src/motor_control.c): R1 site = line 2370, drop '+ (1 << (PID_SHIFT_RIGHT - 1))' and its comment; R2 site = lines 2337-2341, collapse the 'decayed_lpf' correction back to '(low_pass_filtered_error_change * (SCALAR-1)) >> SHIFT'. Comment edits: overflow-bound block line 2136 ('...and the rounding half-LSB sum to at most ~1.8e9') and back-calc comment line 2376-2377 ('|I|+|P|+|D|+half <= ~1.8e9') both name the half-LSB — reword (bounds themselves stay valid; the sum only shrinks by 1024). Line 2137-2138 decay derivation stays numerically valid for sticky decay (verified: sticky fixpoint = exactly 32*max_error_change, never exceeds it; 64e6*31 = 1.984e9 < 2^31). Also bump DEVELOPMENT/BUGFIX version in Src/main.c and rebuild M17+M23(+JIG); new firmware_releases/*.firmware files are git-tracked artifacts.

test_pid_differential.sh (c_test_programs/): the embedded reference model mirrors both — line 152 '+ (1 << 10)' (R1) and line 139 'if (dec < 0) dec += ...' (R2). Any firmware removal without the matching model edit makes the test FAIL immediately on the first tick with a negative lpf or odd-bias sum (that is the test working as designed). Two one-line edits, then re-run (~30 s, 6.5M samples).

test_pid_overflow.c (c_test_programs/): int64 shadow model mirrors both — line 165 '+ (1 << (PID_SHIFT_RIGHT - 1))' (R1), line 148 'if (dec < 0) dec += ...' (R2); header doc comment line 28 states the identity '(I+P+D+half) >> PID_SHIFT_RIGHT'. The lpf-bound invariant at lines 184-186 does NOT need slack after R2 removal: I verified numerically (scratchpad/ultra) that the sticky-decay fixpoint reaches exactly 32*max_error_change and the check is strict '>'. Re-run test_pid_overflow.sh full = 3 product parameter sets (M17 shift 11 / M23 shift 14 / M1-M2 shift 18 + error>>3), ~4-6 min, 3.24B UBSan-checked ticks.

pid_algorithm_sim.c (c_test_programs/): step2 path mirrors both — R1 at lines 272-277 (condition 'ALG_OLD || ALG_STEP1A || o->floor_output' selects floor; step2 default is round-nearest), R2 at lines 217-225 (condition 'ALG_OLD || ALG_STEP1B || o->sticky_decay' selects sticky). Removal inverts the meaning of the --floor-output / --sticky-decay ablation flags (they currently apply OLD behavior to step2+; after removal floor/sticky IS step2, so the flags become no-ops and you'd need opposite-sense flags or delete them, lines 95-96, 467-468). The ALG_STEP1A/STEP1B/STEP1 isolation variants (lines 64-66) become misnomers — 'step1 = old + rounding fixes' stops describing any shipped firmware. Header comment lines 22-27 needs rewording.

run_pid_sim_battery.py (c_test_programs/): R2 removal makes 2 checks FAIL by design — 'step1: D bias eliminated (|mean| < 15k)' and 'step2: D bias eliminated' (lines 89-91; measured sticky bias is ~-85k, threshold 15k). The 'old alg reproduces sticky D bias (mean < -40k)' check (line 87) keeps passing. Report header line 65 ('step2 = rounding fixes + back-calculation anti-windup') needs edit. R1 removal alone is battery-neutral (no check keys on the half-LSB; 'step1 behaves like old' at line 115 compares peak error within 25%). Re-run ~5-10 min (accept the known 60/62 on the pathological plant corners).

run_pid_sim_extended_sweep.sh: no direct R1/R2 dependence (drives --alg step2 with thresholds on post_move_rms/overflow only), but all 82 runs must re-run after the sim edit (~10-15 min) since the step2 semantics change under it.

tools/pid_debug_capture.py: NO functional change needed — detect_shift (lines 306-335) tries BOTH conventions ((p+i+d)>>s floor and (p+i+d+half)>>s round-nearest) for every shift 0..24 per capture, and validation only requires shift 11 to be among the candidates regardless of convention. OLD archived captures (pre-0.15.3.1, floor) and NEW archived captures (0.15.3.1-0.15.3.4, round-nearest) both keep validating unchanged; future floor-firmware captures will be detected as (11, 'floor') and pass. The saturation-consistency exemption (line 323) is algebra-preserving under both conventions ((X - k*2^s)>>s == (X>>s) - k exactly). Only the docstring's version mapping (lines 310-311: 'New firmware (>= 0.15.3.1): round-nearest') becomes misleading and should gain a '(reverted in 0.15.3.5)' note. So: historical-data validation is fully unaffected.

hw_campaign.py (firmware/pid_baseline_captures/2026-07-10_ultracode_pass/): H10 check 'abs(d_mean) < 40000' (line 342) DEPENDS ON R2 — it runs at default kD=175,000 where the sticky bias measures ~-85k pre-shift, so R2 removal makes this hardware gate fail. It would have to be loosened to ~120k or deleted, i.e. weakening a check that exists precisely because the bias was classified a bug (conflicts with the 'fix bugs, not tests' working rule — flag this to Tom explicitly). H10's err_std<80 and post-move rms<200 checks are unaffected (bench measured error std identical, 37.2 vs 37.4, with and without the bias). No H-check depends on R1.

Mutation testing dependence: yes, partially. PID_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md section 16 (lines 945-948) records 8 single-bug mutants including 'rounding' mutants, 16/16 killed. The mutant definitions are ad hoc (nothing on disk; gates_0154.log only says 'MUT1 killed / MUT3 killed'), so nothing breaks in the repo, but after removal any 'delete the rounding' mutant coincides with production code and the spot-check mutant set must be redefined (e.g. 'ADD rounding' becomes the mutant). The differential harness itself still kills mutants fine — it compares against the updated reference model.

PID_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md claims affected: section 2 (lines 119-126) documents the sticky-bias root cause — stays valid as baseline history. Section 6 (lines 424-434) lists both rounding fixes as shipped in 0.15.3.1 and claims the back-calc 'preserves the capture tool's exact identity output == (P+I+D+1024) >> 11' — identity claim must be restated as (P+I+D)>>11. Section 8 (lines 488-494) records the bench D-mean going -80k -> -7k and 'identity now (P+I+D+1024)>>11, detected as round-nearest' — historical, keep but the 'current firmware' narrative needs a new section documenting the removal and re-measured D bias. Section 9 fix list and section 16 ('step2 mirrors all three firmware fixes', 'rounding' mutants) likewise need an addendum, not rewrites. Note Tom's don't-delete-prefer-.bak convention applies to any superseded capture scripts.

Verification gates to re-run and rough wall time: differential (~30 s) + overflow full 3 products (~4-6 min) + battery 62 checks (~5-10 min) + extended sweep 82 runs (~10-15 min) + mutation spot-check with redefined mutants (~5 min) + M17/M23/JIG builds (~5 min) = roughly 25-40 min offline. Bench: flash 0.15.3.5, hw_campaign.py (~20-30 min incl. the 7-min H8 endurance; with H10 rewritten if R2 removed), standstill + move captures re-validated by pid_debug_capture.py (~10 min), full hardware suite run_all_tests.py (~10 min, wrap in a wall-clock timer per working rule) = roughly 1 hour bench. R1-only removal skips the H10/battery check rewrites but still needs every re-run.

Behavior changes beyond the +-1-count / D-bias effects — the honest list is short: (1) R2 removal reinstates a WANDERING (not constant) torque-command offset, mean ~-40 counts of 51,200 authority (~0.08%), which the integrator absorbs when kI>0 (bench: standstill error std 37.2 vs 37.4, i.e. no measurable position benefit at default gains) but which becomes a ~40-count standing position error at kI=0, and re-biases the D-term telemetry that H10 gates on; (2) R1 removal makes PID_controller consistent with PID_controller_debug (line 2284), which never had the half-LSB — a small point IN FAVOR of removal; (3) LPF state bound and all overflow-safety caps remain valid (verified numerically); (4) no product besides M17 defaults changes (M23/M1/M2 share the code, so the same +-1-count/D-bias deltas apply at their shifts 14/18 — the overflow re-run covers them).

KEEP cost, honestly (plan sections 10-11, disassembly-based): R1 = ~4 instructions (materialize + add the half-LSB constant), R2 = ~3 instructions (+2 more only when the filter value is negative), and R2 executes only when kD != 0. Together ~7 of the ~90 common-path instructions in PID_controller, ~= 0.1-0.15 us of the 32 us tick on the 64 MHz M0+ (~0.3-0.5% of ISR budget; measured whole-ISR delta for ALL 0.15.3.x changes was +1-2 us, dominated by the entry clamp and anti-windup, not the rounding). Keeping both is essentially free; removing both buys back roughly one-tenth of a microsecond per tick.
